extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants (SEC-reporting companies), their legal/compliance and investor-relations teams, and preparers of SEC filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final-rule requirements for how SEC registrants must identify and disclose material climate-related risks, the time horizons for those risks, their material impacts on strategy/business model/outlook, and how such impacts are integrated into planning and capital allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and disclose material climate-related risks (physical or transition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that has identified a climate-related risk pursuant to Item 1502 must disclose whether the risk is a physical or transition risk and provide information necessary to an understanding of the nature of the risk presented and the extent of the registrant's exposure to the risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rules provide a non-exclusive list of disclosures the registrant must disclose as applicable; registrants should describe clearly and consistently the climate-related physical or transition risks they face. The particular type of material transition risk disclosed may be one that is not included or only partially included in the definition; not every manifestation will apply to every registrant and risks may change over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical risk disclosure items
rubrics_metrics.description: If a physical risk, disclose whether it may be categorized as an acute or chronic risk, and the geographic location and nature of the properties, processes, or operations subject to the physical risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is non‑exclusive; registrants have flexibility to determine granularity of location disclosures based on facts and circumstances (ZIP/postal-code disclosure not required). Registrants may (but are not required to) discuss interactions among related physical risks (e.g., chronic risks giving rise to acute risks); such interaction discussions can be complex and are optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition risk disclosure items
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transition risk, disclose whether it relates to regulatory, technological, market (including changing consumer, business counterparty, and investor preferences), or other transition-related factors, and how those factors impact the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describing the nature of transition risks in this manner helps investors understand realized or potential material impacts and whether/ how a registrant intends to mitigate or adapt. Registrants with significant operations in jurisdictions that have made GHG commitments should consider whether they are exposed to material transition risk related to implementation of those commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal standard for disclosure (short-term and long-term)
rubrics_metrics.description: When describing climate-related risks that have materially impacted or are reasonably likely to have a material impact, a registrant should state whether such risks are reasonably likely to manifest in the short-term (the next 12 months) and separately in the long-term (beyond the next 12 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is modeled on existing MD&A temporal standards. A registrant is not precluded from further breaking down beyond 12 months (e.g., medium/longer horizons) if consistent with management's assessment. The "reasonably likely" component requires management to evaluate consequences objectively as it would other known trends, events, or uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality determination standard
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating whether climate-related risks have materially impacted or are reasonably likely to have a material impact, registrants should rely on traditional notions of materiality: a matter is material if there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable investor would consider it important in deciding to buy, sell, or vote, or would view omission as significantly altering the total mix of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The materiality determination is fact‑specific and requires both quantitative and qualitative considerations. The standard is the same as generally required when preparing MD&A and requires management to make an objective evaluation, including where fruition of future events is unknown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe actual and potential material impacts on strategy, business model, and outlook (Item 1502(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must describe the actual and potential material impacts of any climate-related risk identified in Item 1502(a) on the registrant's strategy, business model, and outlook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule provides a non‑exclusive list of types of potential material impacts to disclose, as applicable: business operations (including the types and locations of operations); products or services; suppliers, purchasers, or counterparties to material contracts (to the extent known or reasonably available); activities to mitigate or adapt (including adoption of new technologies/processes); and expenditure for research and development. If none of the listed types or any other impacts are material, a registrant need not disclose them. Impacts not specifically listed that are material must still be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits on value-chain related impact disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule limits the scope of value-chain impact disclosure to material impacts on suppliers, purchasers, or counterparties to material contracts, to the extent known or reasonably available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revision addresses concerns about burden and data availability from third parties. The rule is consistent with the Commission's general rules on disclosure of information that is difficult to obtain and is intended to avoid requiring registrants to undertake unreasonable searches or requests for information from their value chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss integration of material impacts into strategy, planning, and capital allocation (Item 1502(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must discuss whether and how it considers any material impacts described under Item 1502(b) as part of its strategy, financial planning, and capital allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As applicable, disclosure should include whether the impacts have been integrated into the business model/strategy (including whether and how resources are being used to mitigate climate-related risks) and how any targets referenced in Item 1504 or in a described transition plan relate to the registrant's business model or strategy. The final rule is less prescriptive than the proposal (e.g., it omits a mandatory requirement to provide both current and forward‑looking disclosures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary disclosure of climate-related opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may elect to disclose any climate-related opportunities they are pursuing or reasonably likely to pursue, but such disclosure is voluntary and not required by the final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules do not include a definition of 'climate-related opportunities' and treat opportunities disclosure the same as other voluntary disclosure; registrants may include such information in addition to required risk disclosures if they choose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles-based / less-prescriptive approach and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules adopt a less-prescriptive, non-exclusive approach intended to elicit registrant‑specific, decision‑useful disclosure while avoiding overly granular or immaterial disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions (e.g., removal of ZIP code and water‑specific metric mandates) were made to reduce burden and avoid investor confusion from immaterial or overly detailed disclosures. Registrants have flexibility to determine which particular metrics or granularity to disclose based on facts and circumstances. Phase‑in periods are provided to allow development of processes and controls.
